title: Build a balanced release
effort: Accelerate a ball through a controlled body turn into a balanced projection.

exercises.name: Med Ball Rotational Scoop Toss — paused standing start; floor-target adaptation
exercises.sourceName: Med Ball Rotational Scoop Toss — paused standing start; floor-target adaptation
exercises.purpose: Primary anchor: generate rotational projection from a settled load.
exercises.instruction: Stand side-on, feet at a comfortable athletic width; hold the ball near the rear hip and pause 2 seconds. Pivot the rear foot, turn the hips/trunk, and sweep both hands through the target. No preparatory bounce or step. Finish balanced for 2 seconds. Reduce ball mass or turn range if the arms lead or the athlete spins out.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Rotational Med Ball Throw
exercises.sourceName: Half-Kneeling Rotational Med Ball Throw — floor-target adaptation
exercises.purpose: Express trunk-to-hand acceleration with leg propulsion reduced.
exercises.instruction: Target-side foot forward, opposite knee comfortably supported on the floor; ball begins beside the rear hip. Use a small comfortable thoracic turn and fast two-hand release; do not force the pelvis to remain rigid while twisting farther. Keep the front foot planted and pelvis quiet. Shorten the turn if the knee shifts or back arches; use a seated bench rotational throw instead of this slot if kneeling contact is intolerable.

exercises.name: Med Ball Countermovement Rotational Throw
exercises.sourceName: Med Ball Countermovement Rotational Throw — floor-target adaptation
exercises.purpose: Change a brief preload immediately into the same projection.
exercises.instruction: Standing side-on, make one small, smooth wind-back and reverse promptly into the throw; no pause, repeated rocking or extra step. This differs from E1's settled start. Keep the wind-back small enough that the trunk stays controlled. Reduce its amplitude if the athlete overtwists or delays the reversal.

exercises.name: Med Ball Shot-Put Throw — rotational, floor-target adaptation
exercises.sourceName: Med Ball Shot-Put Throw — rotational, floor-target adaptation
exercises.purpose: Finish the turn with a unilateral pushing release.
exercises.instruction: Stagger the feet with the nonthrowing foot forward. Support the light ball at the rear shoulder with the other hand, turn through the rear foot/hip, then drive the throwing hand forward; the support hand guides and releases. Do not wind the arm behind the shoulder or turn it into an overhead baseball throw. Use a smaller/lighter grippable ball if wrist position or speed is lost.

exercises.name: Med Ball Step-Behind Rotational Throw
exercises.sourceName: Med Ball Step-Behind Rotational Throw — floor-target adaptation
exercises.purpose: Transfer a short weight shift into upper-body rotation without continued travel.
exercises.instruction: From side-on, make one small step behind, replant the lead foot and deliver a scoop release. Keep total approach travel within 1 m, both feet grounded at release and the finish inside the start bay. No running, hop or jump. Use a simple step-in rotational throw instead of the crossover version if foot placement is unreliable; retain 1 × 2 per direction and record the replacement.

exercises.name: Med Ball Overhead to Side Slam
exercises.sourceName: Med Ball Overhead to Side Slam — non-rebounding slam-ball execution
exercises.purpose: Accelerate the hands diagonally downward through a turn and arrest the body's follow-through.
exercises.instruction: From a comfortable overhead position, turn through the feet/hips and drive the ball to the floor slightly forward and outside the target-side foot, clear of toes. Stay long through the trunk; do not fold and twist at the low back. Lift/reset deliberately after the ball stops. Use a shoulder-height diagonal side slam instead of the overhead version if overhead range requires rib flare; same dose.

exercises.name: Split-Stance Pallof Press — light band
exercises.dose: 1 × 5 per anchor side, 2-second extension hold; 10 reps / 20 seconds held
exercises.purpose: Maintain the stacked finish against an external turning pull.
exercises.instruction: Band at sternum height to the side; mirror the anchor-facing side and lead foot. Press forward without the ribs or pelvis turning toward the anchor, breathe during the hold, return in 2 seconds. Use a shorter reach or lighter band instead if the torso drifts.

exercises.name: Side-lying dumbbell external rotation
exercises.sourceName: Side-lying dumbbell external rotation — proposed addition
exercises.purpose: Load controlled shoulder external rotation after the throwing exposure and before pressing.
exercises.instruction: Lie on the opposite side with the working elbow bent 90 degrees and resting at the ribs. Rotate the forearm up through a comfortable range in 2 seconds; lower in 3 seconds. Keep the elbow at the ribs and trunk still. Use less load/range if the shoulder shrugs or the torso rolls. This is intended shoulder control work, not a claim of injury prevention.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
exercises.dose: 2 × 6 alternating side-to-side traverses; 3 each direction per set, 12 total
exercises.purpose: Main strength anchor: resist and drive the loaded turning arc used to deliver the ball.
exercises.instruction: Secure the landmine; hold the sleeve/appropriate grip in both hands, elbows softly bent, and use a modest side-to-side arc. Feet and hips turn with the load; keep ribs over pelvis. One one-way traverse is one rep; the return is the next rep, not an uncounted return. Use about 2 seconds per traverse and settle briefly at each end. Rest 2–3 minutes between working sets. Reduce load/arc for a trunk lean, knee twist or uncontrolled endpoint.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotational Press
exercises.rest: 90 s between sides · 2 min between rounds
exercises.purpose: Strengthen the link from body turn to unilateral pressing force.
exercises.instruction: Start in a modest staggered stance, sleeve near the rear shoulder; pivot the rear foot and turn into a controlled forward/up press. No dip-drive, jump or release. Return in 3 seconds; keep the shoulder away from the ear. Rest 90 seconds between sides; 2 minutes between rounds. Reduce load if the elbow/wrist collapses or the lower back supplies the finish.

exercises.name: Standing rotational band row
exercises.sourceName: Standing rotational band row — proposed band variant of Rotational Cable Row
exercises.purpose: Load the pulling side of the turn and control the return into the next preload.
exercises.instruction: Band anchored in front at lower-chest height, opposite foot forward; reach without rounding, then turn feet/hips/trunk modestly as the elbow draws toward the same-side lower ribs. Return in 3 seconds under band tension. This is a single rotational row, not a row-plus-twist combination. Rest 90 seconds between sides. Reduce tension if the shoulder hikes or the athlete yanks from the low back.

exercises.name: Band Chop
exercises.sourceName: Cable / Band Chop — standing split-stance band execution
exercises.purpose: Strengthen the high-to-low diagonal that finishes E6 and controls the downward release path.
exercises.instruction: High band anchor to one side; opposite foot forward, both hands travel from above that shoulder toward the opposite front pocket. Allow the feet/hips to turn while keeping the trunk long. Drive in 1–2 seconds; return in 3 seconds. Rest 90 seconds between sides. Reduce resistance/range if the athlete crunches sideways or the band recoils.

exercises.name: Band Lift
exercises.sourceName: Cable / Band Lift — standing split-stance band execution
exercises.purpose: Strengthen the low-to-high hand path from the loaded rear hip toward the forward release position.
exercises.instruction: Low band anchor to the rear side; move both hands from that hip across to opposite upper-chest height, allowing a small foot/hip turn. Do not lift above the range that retains rib position. Drive in 1–2 seconds and return in 3 seconds. Rest 90 seconds between sides. Reduce range/tension if leaning back replaces rotation.

exercises.name: Single-arm Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.sourceName: Single-arm Dumbbell Floor Press — proposed unilateral variant
exercises.purpose: Load terminal horizontal pressing force for E4 after rotation has brought the arm forward.
exercises.instruction: Lie supine, feet comfortably planted, one dumbbell above the chest; lower in 3 seconds until the upper arm gently meets the floor, pause briefly and press. Keep ribs/pelvis level; no bridge or torso roll. Rest 90 seconds between sides. This isolates the release-side press more than P2's integrated upward arc; one working set limits overlap. Use less load if the elbow lands hard or the trunk rolls.

quality: During E1's twelve scheduled attempts, record each side's valid attempts: controlled rear-foot pivot and hip initiation, hands following the turn, release into the declared target zone, and a balanced two-second finish without an extra recovery step. Record the specific fault on unsuccessful attempts; they still count as exposure. This is a coaching observation, not a measurement of force or an established pass-rate test. Do not add attempts for assessment.
preparation: P1: 1 × 4 alternating traverses with a lighter load. P2: 1 × 4 per arm lighter. P3–P6: 1 × 3 per side lighter at that exercise's working tempo. Allow 30–45 seconds to change sides during these easy sets, then 60–90 seconds before the first working set. If another preparation set is necessary for P1 or P2, repeat its stated easy dose, log it and allow extra time. Preparation sets must not become challenging work. These are load checks for the listed lifts, not a replacement preparation sequence.
explosiveNotes:
Exactly 6 exercises. Use light, grippable balls that permit a visibly fast release with controlled posture. Select by demonstrated execution, not an age-based kilogram prescription. Each attempt is one release followed by a full reset; no rebound catches, repeated slams or return throws. The first scheduled attempt may establish an appropriate ball and range; it is included in the dose.

Throwing setup applies to E1–E5: Use the floor-target adaptation described below: a low forward release into a cone-marked floor target, initially about 2–3 m downrange, using an impact-compatible ball with verified low rebound. This is rotational projection practice, not maximum-distance testing. Mirror the stance while keeping every release down the same cleared lane. A throwing wall is unconfirmed. Do not reinterpret a listed ball as proof that a safe throwing surface or suitable rebound behavior exists.

Recovery for every row: Allow 10–15 seconds between releases for retrieval/reset, longer if needed; rest 90 seconds after each side's set before the next side/set/exercise. A round means complete one side, rest, complete the other side. For E1, rest again before the second round. Retrieval and transition can occur within rest; count elapsed time once. Stand clear until the ball stops and the coach releases the area.

title: Turn into a pushing release
effort: Turn a stable base into a fast pushing release, then control the arm finish.

exercises.name: Light-band rotational cross
exercises.purpose: Primary: transmit the turn into a fast forward punch.
exercises.instruction: From a modest staggered stance, anchor behind the rear shoulder; turn the rear foot/hip then drive the hand forward at shoulder height. Stop short of locked elbow and return under control; never release the band. Reduce tension or reach if the wrist folds or arm leads the turn. Rest 90 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Rotational shadow hook
exercises.purpose: Coordinate a short transverse hand arc with the trunk turn.
exercises.instruction: With no implement or target, keep elbow bent near 90 degrees and fist between chest and shoulder height; pivot and swing the forearm as a compact unit, stopping near the midline. Reset fully. Shorten the arc if the fist outruns the trunk or shoulder rolls forward. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Two-hand band backhand speed sweep
exercises.sourceName: Two-hand band backhand speed sweep [Proposed addition/variant]
exercises.purpose: Accelerate the transverse pulling/sweeping path while controlling its endpoint.
exercises.instruction: Anchor at chest height on the starting side. Both hands begin near that side of the chest; pivot and sweep across toward the opposite side with softly bent elbows, stopping within a comfortable arc. Return slowly. Reduce tension/arc for side bending or a jerky return. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Medicine Ball Shot-Put Throw
exercises.sourceName: Half-Kneeling Medicine Ball Shot-Put Throw — floor target
exercises.purpose: Express release-side pressing with leg drive reduced.
exercises.instruction: Target-side foot forward, rear knee comfortably grounded. Support the ball beside the rear shoulder; use a small comfortable trunk turn then push it toward the low forward target with the rear hand. Guide hand releases first. Use a lighter grippable ball or smaller turn if the knee shifts or back arches. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Standing rotational two-hand chest push throw
exercises.sourceName: Standing rotational two-hand chest push throw [Proposed addition/variant]
exercises.purpose: Deliver the turn through simultaneous horizontal arm extension.
exercises.instruction: Hold a light ball near the rear side of the chest with both hands. Turn the feet/hips and press both hands through the verified low forward target; do not scoop from the hip. Reduce ball mass if the athlete bends sideways or lets one hand take over. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Two-hand transverse battle-rope whip
exercises.purpose: Apply a brief rotational impulse against rope inertia, then brake.
exercises.instruction: Facing the rope anchor in an athletic stance, hold one rope end in each hand; shift both hands from beside one hip across to the other with a small foot/hip turn. One directed sweep is one rep; settle the rope and walk hands back slowly before the next. Use the stated band-sweep replacement if rope mass or anchor fit prevents a fast controlled impulse. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Scapular Push-Up
exercises.purpose: Control the shoulder blade that must transmit punching force.
exercises.instruction: Use hands on a secured bench if needed. Keep elbows straight but soft; allow a small controlled chest sink between shoulders, then push the support away without rounding the low back. Use 2 seconds each way. Use a higher stable hand support instead if trunk position fails.

exercises.name: Side Plank — short-lever light hold
exercises.dose: 1 × 1 holds of 15 s per side/direction; 2 holds
exercises.purpose: Resist sideways trunk drift during the hand finish.
exercises.instruction: Support on forearm and bent knees; elbow under shoulder, hips stacked. Lift hips and breathe while holding 15 seconds; stop before shaking changes alignment. Shorten hold or reduce hip lift if the shoulder shrugs or pelvis rolls.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotational Press
exercises.rest: 90 s between sides · 2 min between rounds
exercises.purpose: Load the turn-to-forward/up press link.
exercises.instruction: Rear hand holds the sleeve at the rear shoulder in a modest staggered stance. Pivot the rear foot and turn into a forward/up press without a dip-drive or release. Return in 3 seconds, wrist stacked and ribs level. Use less load for rib flare or elbow/wrist collapse; if minimum bar load is unsuitable, use a rotational band press instead at this dose.

exercises.name: Single-arm Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.rest: 90 s between sides · 2 min between rounds
exercises.purpose: Load terminal horizontal pressing after the turn.
exercises.instruction: Lie supine with feet comfortably planted and one dumbbell over the chest. Lower in 3 seconds until the upper arm gently meets the floor, briefly pause and press. Keep ribs/pelvis level; no bridge or roll. Use less load if the elbow lands hard or the trunk rolls.

exercises.name: Standing rotational band row
exercises.purpose: Strengthen the pulling side that organizes the opposing shoulder.
exercises.instruction: Band fixed in front at lower-chest height, opposite foot forward. Turn feet/hips/trunk modestly while drawing the elbow toward the same-side lower ribs; return in 3 seconds. Keep the shoulder down and trunk long. Reduce band tension/turn range if the shoulder hikes or the athlete yanks from the low back.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
exercises.purpose: Retain loaded turning strength without a second high-volume trunk task.
exercises.instruction: Use both hands and softly bent elbows. Turn feet/hips with a modest side-to-side arc; keep ribs over pelvis. One one-way traverse is one rep and the reverse is the next rep; six alternating traverses contain three per direction. Take about 2 seconds per traverse and settle briefly at the endpoint. Reduce arc/load if the knee twists, trunk leans or endpoint runs away.

exercises.name: Band Chop
exercises.sourceName: Cable / Band Chop — standing band execution
exercises.purpose: Control the diagonal finish when the arm begins to drift upward.
exercises.instruction: Secure a high band anchor to the side; opposite foot forward. Both hands travel from above that shoulder toward the opposite front pocket, with a small foot/hip turn. Drive in 1–2 seconds and return in 3. Reduce range/tension if sideways crunching or band recoil replaces control.

exercises.name: Band Lift
exercises.sourceName: Cable / Band Lift — standing band execution
exercises.purpose: Strengthen the path from rear hip toward the pressing platform.
exercises.instruction: Secure a low band anchor to the rear side. Move both hands from the rear hip across to opposite upper-chest height, allowing feet/hips to turn. Drive in 1–2 seconds and return in 3; stop below rib flare. Reduce range/tension if leaning back supplies the lift.

quality: For E1 record whether the rear-foot pivot/hip turn precedes the hand, the wrist stays straight, the elbow remains softly extended and the athlete returns to the same stance without a recovery step on each scheduled attempt. Observe during the scheduled anchor attempts, count all attempted work, and do not add testing reps. A different drill is not a comparable performance test or evidence of improvement.
preparation: Before each listed primary lift, perform one easy set of 3 per side using lighter resistance; for alternating Landmine Rotation use 4 traverses total instead. These are the same six exercises, not additional slots. Allow 30–45 s to change sides and 60–90 s before working. Minimum preparation is 34 easy reps in 11 bouts, separate from working work. If another preparation set is needed, repeat that lift's easy dose, log it and add the time. No max tests or forced reps. Secure band anchors and landmine; if the minimum bar is unsuitable, use the same-dose standing two-hand band rotation or one-arm rotational band press instead of the relevant landmine lift, recording the proposed replacement.
explosiveNotes: Exactly six exercises. E1 receives two sets; other drills receive one small set per side. No target is struck and no partner contact is permitted. Use light implements and fast coordinated intent; a retained-load drill ends under control rather than being released. Both sides receive the written dose.

title: Reverse the preload
effort: Reverse a compact preload into rotational hand speed without a second wind-up.

exercises.name: Med Ball Countermovement Rotational Throw
exercises.sourceName: Med Ball Countermovement Rotational Throw — floor target
exercises.purpose: Primary: turn one compact preload immediately into release.
exercises.instruction: Stand side-on with a light ball near the rear hip; make one small wind-back then reverse into a two-hand scoop release. Feet may pivot; no entry step or repeated rocking. Hold the finish for 2 seconds. Reduce wind-back range if the athlete pauses, overtwists or loses direction. Rest 90 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Countermovement rotational shot-put throw
exercises.purpose: Apply prompt reversal to a unilateral pressing release.
exercises.instruction: Ball supported beside the rear shoulder; allow one small backward body turn, then pivot forward and push toward the low target with the rear hand. Keep the elbow below shoulder height and guide hand relaxed. Reduce the preload or ball mass if the wrist collapses or the arm winds behind the torso. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Rotational band row speed drive
exercises.sourceName: Rotational band row speed drive [Proposed addition/variant]
exercises.purpose: Accelerate the pulling side of the turn without jerking the shoulder.
exercises.instruction: Light band anchored ahead at lower-chest height. From a controlled reach, pivot/turn and draw the elbow toward lower ribs quickly; stop cleanly and return in 3 seconds. One pull-return is one rep. Reduce tension/reach if the shoulder hikes or the trunk yanks backward. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Two-hand diagonal battle-rope chop pulse
exercises.sourceName: Two-hand diagonal battle-rope chop pulse [Proposed addition/variant]
exercises.purpose: Reverse an elevated preload into a brief downward rotational impulse.
exercises.instruction: With a light manageable rope pair, start hands near one shoulder; pivot and drive both ends diagonally toward the opposite hip. Settle the rope completely and reset deliberately before another pulse. Use the stated diagonal band-pull replacement if rope weight or clearance prevents clean speed. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Two-hand medicine-ball backhand throw
exercises.purpose: Express outward transverse force without relying on elbow extension.
exercises.instruction: Begin hands across the front of the body near the opposite lower ribs, elbows softly bent. Turn toward the cleared lane and sweep both hands outward at waist-to-chest height into the low target. Reset without receiving a rebound. Shorten the sweep if the ball drags the shoulder behind the torso. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Rotational shadow uppercut
exercises.purpose: Link a compact turn to an upward bent-arm hand path.
exercises.instruction: No target or implement. With elbow bent, move the fist from lower-rib height toward chin height as the rear foot/hip turns; stop before the shoulder shrugs. No deep squat or overhead punch. Shorten the upward path if the low back extends or the arm separates from the turn. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Bear Position Shoulder Tap
exercises.purpose: Maintain trunk position while support briefly shifts to one arm.
exercises.instruction: Hands below shoulders, knees just clear of the floor. Slowly lift one hand to touch the opposite shoulder, replace it, then alternate; pelvis stays level. Take about 3 seconds each rep. Use knees on the floor instead if the pelvis sways; keep the same slow tap dose.

exercises.name: Band-Resisted Dead Bug Pullover
exercises.purpose: Keep ribs controlled while the arms lengthen into the next preload.
exercises.instruction: Lie supine with knees bent and feet supported; light band anchored securely beyond the head. Move both hands from above the face toward the ribs, then return slowly without arching. This is one arm-pullover task; do not add alternating leg extensions. Reduce overhead reach/tension if the ribs lift.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
exercises.purpose: Strengthen the turning arc that must reverse under control.
exercises.instruction: Use both hands and softly bent elbows. Turn feet/hips with a modest side-to-side arc; keep ribs over pelvis. One one-way traverse is one rep and the reverse is the next rep; six alternating traverses contain three per direction. Take about 2 seconds per traverse and settle briefly at the endpoint. Reduce arc/load if the knee twists, trunk leans or endpoint runs away.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row — supported
exercises.purpose: Load scapular pulling force while the trunk supplies a stable platform.
exercises.instruction: Support the free hand on a stable bench, feet staggered. Row the dumbbell toward the same-side hip without turning the torso; lower in 3 seconds. Use less load if the shoulder hikes or the trunk rotates.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotational Press
exercises.purpose: Preserve force through the unilateral release-side press.
exercises.instruction: Rear hand holds the sleeve at the rear shoulder in a modest staggered stance. Pivot the rear foot and turn into a forward/up press without a dip-drive or release. Return in 3 seconds, wrist stacked and ribs level. Use less load for rib flare or elbow/wrist collapse; if minimum bar load is unsuitable, use a rotational band press instead at this dose.

exercises.name: Band Chop
exercises.sourceName: Cable / Band Chop — standing band execution
exercises.purpose: Load the downward diagonal and its controlled return.
exercises.instruction: Secure a high band anchor to the side; opposite foot forward. Both hands travel from above that shoulder toward the opposite front pocket, with a small foot/hip turn. Drive in 1–2 seconds and return in 3. Reduce range/tension if sideways crunching or band recoil replaces control.

exercises.name: Band Lift
exercises.sourceName: Cable / Band Lift — standing band execution
exercises.purpose: Load the opposite diagonal that establishes the preload.
exercises.instruction: Secure a low band anchor to the rear side. Move both hands from the rear hip across to opposite upper-chest height, allowing feet/hips to turn. Drive in 1–2 seconds and return in 3; stop below rib flare. Reduce range/tension if leaning back supplies the lift.

exercises.name: Single-arm Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.purpose: Maintain terminal pressing strength with limited added volume.
exercises.instruction: Lie supine with feet comfortably planted and one dumbbell over the chest. Lower in 3 seconds until the upper arm gently meets the floor, briefly pause and press. Keep ribs/pelvis level; no bridge or roll. Use less load if the elbow lands hard or the trunk rolls.

quality: For E1 note whether one small wind-back flows directly into the release, without a pause, second rock, added step or exaggerated lumbar turn. Count balanced two-second finishes on each side within scheduled attempts. Observe during the scheduled anchor attempts, count all attempted work, and do not add testing reps. A different drill is not a comparable performance test or evidence of improvement.
preparation: Before each listed primary lift, perform one easy set of 3 per side using lighter resistance; for alternating Landmine Rotation use 4 traverses total instead. These are the same six exercises, not additional slots. Allow 30–45 s to change sides and 60–90 s before working. Minimum preparation is 34 easy reps in 11 bouts, separate from working work. If another preparation set is needed, repeat that lift's easy dose, log it and add the time. No max tests or forced reps. Secure band anchors and landmine; if the minimum bar is unsuitable, use the same-dose standing two-hand band rotation or one-arm rotational band press instead of the relevant landmine lift, recording the proposed replacement.
explosiveNotes: Exactly six exercises. The reversal anchor receives 2 × 3 per side; other tasks are 1 × 3 per side. Maintain a small preload; do not chase a larger range. Use light implements and fast coordinated intent; a retained-load drill ends under control rather than being released. Both sides receive the written dose.

title: Step, plant & project
effort: Deliver rotational force through the hand after a short deliberate step, without losing the release line.

exercises.name: Step-in rotational medicine-ball shot-put
exercises.purpose: Primary: turn a deliberate plant into a directed pushing release.
exercises.instruction: Start staggered with ball at the rear shoulder; take one small lead-foot step toward the low forward target, settle that foot, pivot the rear hip and press the ball with the rear hand. Hold the finish. Use the standing rotational shot-put instead at the same dose if a step causes falling or knee twist. Rest 90 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Light-band rotational uppercut
exercises.purpose: Apply the turn to an upward hand path against retained resistance.
exercises.instruction: Band secured low behind the working side, hand near the hip. With bent elbow, pivot the rear foot and drive the fist toward upper-chest height; stop below shoulder shrug and return slowly. Reduce tension/height if the trunk arches or band pulls the wrist out of line. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: One-Arm Landmine Arc Press — light fast arc
exercises.sourceName: One-Arm Landmine Arc Press — light fast arc
exercises.purpose: Control the release-side shoulder through a rapid guided transverse arc.
exercises.instruction: Start sleeve in one hand in front of the same-side upper chest, elbow softly bent. Sweep a short arc toward the opposite upper chest with a small body turn, maintaining safe bar clearance; return deliberately. No release or overhead circle. Use the stated unloaded transverse sweep replacement if the bar is too heavy for speed/control. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Lead-hand rotational medicine-ball push throw
exercises.sourceName: Lead-hand rotational medicine-ball push throw [Proposed addition/variant]
exercises.rest: the target without a large rear-arm wind-up
exercises.purpose: Express force through the arm nearest the target without a large rear-arm wind-up.
exercises.instruction: Use a very light ball held at the lead-side chest with the other hand assisting its support. Make a small turn toward the lane and extend the lead arm into the low target; the supporting hand releases. Keep both feet planted/pivoting. Use a smaller grippable ball or shorten the turn if the lead shoulder rolls forward. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Two-hand rotational overhead medicine-ball throw
exercises.sourceName: Two-hand rotational overhead medicine-ball throw [Proposed addition/variant]
exercises.purpose: Transfer the turn through a comfortable elevated arm position.
exercises.instruction: Hold a light ball above the forehead, not behind the neck. Turn feet/hips toward the lane and throw forward/down through the cleared target while keeping ribs stacked. One release, full reset. Use the stated rotational chest-push replacement if overhead position requires arching. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Rotational shadow hook
exercises.purpose: Rehearse a compact connected hand arc without additional implement stress.
exercises.instruction: No target or implement. Pivot the rear foot and sweep the bent forearm at chest height as one compact unit with the trunk; stop near midline, then reset. Shorten the arc if the hand leads the body or shoulder rolls forward. Rest 60 s between side bouts/sets.

exercises.name: Band Anti-Rotation Walkout
exercises.purpose: Keep the torso stable while the base changes under a sideways pull.
exercises.instruction: Light band at sternum height from the side; hold hands near the chest. Take one short step away, pause 2 seconds without turning, then return. One out-and-back is one rep; mirror sides. Use a smaller step or less tension if the hips shift or breath is held.

exercises.name: Supine single-arm dumbbell serratus reach
exercises.sourceName: Supine single-arm dumbbell serratus reach [Proposed addition/variant]
exercises.purpose: Control the shoulder blade near the end of a forward press.
exercises.instruction: Lie supine with one light dumbbell above the shoulder and elbow softly straight. Reach the hand slightly upward by moving the shoulder blade, then lower the blade in 2 seconds; keep torso flat. Reduce load/reach if the elbow bends or trunk rolls.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotational Press
exercises.rest: 90 s between sides · 2 min between rounds
exercises.purpose: Load plant-to-turn-to-press force transfer.
exercises.instruction: Rear hand holds the sleeve at the rear shoulder in a modest staggered stance. Pivot the rear foot and turn into a forward/up press without a dip-drive or release. Return in 3 seconds, wrist stacked and ribs level. Use less load for rib flare or elbow/wrist collapse; if minimum bar load is unsuitable, use a rotational band press instead at this dose.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
exercises.purpose: Maintain the turning arc without added entry fatigue.
exercises.instruction: Use both hands and softly bent elbows. Turn feet/hips with a modest side-to-side arc; keep ribs over pelvis. One one-way traverse is one rep and the reverse is the next rep; six alternating traverses contain three per direction. Take about 2 seconds per traverse and settle briefly at the endpoint. Reduce arc/load if the knee twists, trunk leans or endpoint runs away.

exercises.name: Standing rotational band row
exercises.purpose: Organize the pulling shoulder during the hand finish.

exercises.name: Side-lying dumbbell external rotation
exercises.purpose: Revisit shoulder rotational control before the loaded references.
exercises.instruction: Lie on the nonworking side, working elbow at ribs and bent 90 degrees. Raise the forearm through comfortable external rotation in 2 seconds; lower in 3, keeping torso still. Use less load/range if the shoulder shrugs or trunk rolls.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
exercises.purpose: Original loaded reference: controlled turning arc and endpoints.
exercises.instruction: Use both hands and softly bent elbows. Turn feet/hips with a modest side-to-side arc; keep ribs over pelvis. One one-way traverse is one rep and the reverse is the next rep; six alternating traverses contain three per direction. Take about 2 seconds per traverse and settle briefly at the endpoint. Reduce arc/load if the knee twists, trunk leans or endpoint runs away.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotational Press
exercises.rest: 90 s between sides · 2 min between rounds
exercises.purpose: Original loaded reference: body turn connected to the arm press.
exercises.instruction: Rear hand holds the sleeve at the rear shoulder in a modest staggered stance. Pivot the rear foot and turn into a forward/up press without a dip-drive or release. Return in 3 seconds, wrist stacked and ribs level. Use less load for rib flare or elbow/wrist collapse; if minimum bar load is unsuitable, use a rotational band press instead at this dose.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row — supported
exercises.purpose: Support the pulling shoulder while avoiding a duplicate speed-row prescription.
exercises.instruction: Free hand on a stable bench, feet staggered. Row toward the same-side hip while the torso stays quiet, then lower in 3 seconds. Use less load if shrugging or torso rotation appears.

exercises.name: Band Chop
exercises.sourceName: Cable / Band Chop — standing band execution
exercises.purpose: Maintain downward diagonal strength at a support dose.
exercises.instruction: Secure a high band anchor to the side; opposite foot forward. Both hands travel from above that shoulder toward the opposite front pocket, with a small foot/hip turn. Drive in 1–2 seconds and return in 3. Reduce range/tension if sideways crunching or band recoil replaces control.

exercises.name: Band Lift
exercises.sourceName: Cable / Band Lift — standing band execution
exercises.purpose: Maintain upward diagonal strength and controlled preload.
exercises.instruction: Secure a low band anchor to the rear side. Move both hands from the rear hip across to opposite upper-chest height, allowing feet/hips to turn. Drive in 1–2 seconds and return in 3; stop below rib flare. Reduce range/tension if leaning back supplies the lift.

exercises.name: Single-arm Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.purpose: Maintain terminal pressing force without another heavy compound test.
exercises.instruction: Lie supine with feet comfortably planted and one dumbbell over the chest. Lower in 3 seconds until the upper arm gently meets the floor, briefly pause and press. Keep ribs/pelvis level; no bridge or roll. Use less load if the elbow lands hard or the trunk rolls.

quality: For E1 use the Class 1 observation rule: rear-foot pivot/hip initiation, hands following the turn, release into the declared target and a balanced two-second finish without another recovery step. Compare only actual records with the same ball, stance, pause, target, side order, rest and scoring. If earlier actual records are absent, label this the first observed reference; no improvement claim. Observe during the scheduled anchor attempts, count all attempted work, and do not add testing reps. A different drill is not a comparable performance test or evidence of improvement.
preparation: Before each listed primary lift, perform one easy set of 3 per side using lighter resistance; for alternating Landmine Rotation use 4 traverses total instead. These are the same six exercises, not additional slots. Allow 30–45 s to change sides and 60–90 s before working. Class 12 exception: for Landmine Rotational Press use 1 × 4 easy reps per arm instead of 3, matching Class 1; other listed preparation rules stand. Minimum preparation is 36 easy reps in 11 bouts, separate from working work. If another preparation set is needed, repeat that lift's easy dose, log it and add the time. No max tests or forced reps. Secure band anchors and landmine; if the minimum bar is unsuitable, use the same-dose standing two-hand band rotation or one-arm rotational band press instead of the relevant landmine lift, recording the proposed replacement.
explosiveNotes: Exactly six exercises. E1 exactly repeats Class 1’s 2 × 3 per side, including 90-second between-side/set recovery. E2 is only 1 × 2 per side; the other reference/support doses are modest. No extra test attempts, catch circuits or maximum-load tests. Use light implements and fast coordinated intent; a retained-load drill ends under control rather than being released. Both sides receive the written dose.
